entry.summary: Visa-free short stays as part of the Schengen area.
entry.max_stay: 90 days in any 180-day period across the Schengen area
entry.pre_arrival: None today. ETIAS is on the watch list.
entry.other: Get a clear entry stamp on first Schengen entry; airlines may refuse boarding without proof of entry. AIMA, Portugal's immigration agency, has a large backlog. Schengen Entry/Exit System: fingerprints and photo at the border on first entry (free, nothing to do beforehand). Get an entry stamp where one is still given, and carry your passport across internal borders.

tourism.detail: Australians are generally visa-exempt for short Schengen stays.
tourism.next: Check the current Schengen and Portuguese border requirements.

meetings.detail: Meetings, negotiations, fairs and conferences can fit a visitor trip where no Portuguese service delivery occurs.
meetings.next: Carry host letter, event ticket and business purpose.

conference.detail: Delegate entry is distinct from paid programme delivery, training or local event work.
conference.next: Ask the organiser to label your role and payment.

unpaid-speaking.route: Host classification for invited cultural/academic activity
unpaid-speaking.detail: A free talk may be cultural or professional activity depending on host, expenses and duties; visitor entry is not a universal speaker permit.
unpaid-speaking.next: Have the host ask AIMA/consulate if the exact event is exempt or needs residence/work permission.

paid-speaking.route: Portuguese work/residence permit or independent activity route
paid-speaking.detail: Paid speaking, consulting and training can be employment or independent activity and should be documented before arrival.
paid-speaking.next: Separate one-off event delivery from a local contract or recurring activity.

book-launch.detail: Rights meetings may fit business travel; launches, readings, signings, workshops and local book sales can add work and tax obligations.
book-launch.next: List fee, royalties, reimbursement and retail separately.

ai-teaching.route: Academic/research host or local work route
ai-teaching.detail: A university invitation and an independent commercial workshop are different activity shapes.
ai-teaching.next: Ask the institution or client to choose the correct visa/residence basis.

remote-work.detail: AIMA publishes residence for remote professional activity performed for entities outside Portugal, subject to income, accommodation and other evidence.
remote-work.next: Check the current D8 checklist and keep Portuguese clients/local delivery separate.

entrepreneur.route: D2 independent activity, startup or investment residence
entrepreneur.detail: Portugal offers residence routes for independent activity, entrepreneurship and qualifying investment; AIMA evidence and current programme rules matter.
entrepreneur.next: Choose D2/startup/investment and build the Portuguese project file.

trade.route: Short business visit; Portuguese operation needs local status
trade.detail: Sourcing, negotiation and fairs can be visitor activity; local fulfilment or service delivery may not be.
trade.next: State where the contract, invoice and delivery occur.

artist.detail: Paid performance, literary appearances and production work need host contracts and the appropriate activity status.
artist.next: Have the producer specify venue, fee, royalties and local labour.

mixed-mission.route: Schengen entry plus D8/D2 or host activation
mixed-mission.detail: Portugal can support a quick arrival and a longer base, but each paid/local activity remains separately classified.
mixed-mission.next: Build one schedule with foreign remote work, Portuguese work and cultural activity separated.

filming.route: Visa-free Schengen short stay (journalistic or media purposes)
filming.detail: Journalistic or media purposes are listed among visa-free purposes; paid production work and location permits are national matters.
filming.next: Ask the Embassy of Portugal, DEAKIN about filming, and the local authority about locations.

research.route: Visa-free Schengen short stay (short-term study or training)
research.detail: Short-term study and training are covered; paid research at an institution is paid activity.
research.next: Ask the Embassy of Portugal, DEAKIN if the host pays you.

volunteering.detail: Volunteering isn't addressed in the EU guidance read.
volunteering.next: Ask the Embassy of Portugal, DEAKIN.

laws.rule: Possession and use of illegal drugs are administrative offences and can attract large fines. Selling or trafficking illegal drugs is a criminal offence. Penalties are severe and can include jail sentences.
laws.heading: Drugs

laws.rule: Gambling is legal in venues licensed by the government, such as official casinos. Gambling is illegal in unlicensed venues. Organisers, players and anyone on the premises may be charged, fined or jailed. Check you're entering a licensed gambling venue.
laws.heading: Gambling

laws.rule: A Code of Conduct has been introduced in the municipality of Albufeira, in the Algarve, banning inappropriate behaviour in public places. Be aware of the rules and avoid on the spot fines ranging between €150 and €1,800.
laws.heading: Inappropriate behaviour in public places

laws.rule: You must carry photo ID. You may be required to pay IVA (VAT/GST) and/or customs fees to receive international parcels via mail, including online shopping and gifts. Fees may seem high relative to the value of goods, and you may be asked to attend a customs facility or pay an agent to release goods.
laws.heading: Other laws

laws.rule: You can carry prescription medicines for personal use into Portugal. If you are unsure about medication and quantities, contact the Portuguese National Drug Authority, Infarmed. To receive medications by post, you may require an import permit.
laws.heading: Medication

laws.rule: You can drive using a valid Australian driver's licence. Local authorities and car rental companies require the presentation of an original driver licence. Australian digital driver licences are not accepted. If you hold a residence permit for Portugal, you can continue to use your valid Australian driver's license as long as you meet certain conditions.
laws.heading: Driving permit

money-and-cost.cash_card_notes: The local currency is the euro (EUR). Declare amounts over 10,000 euros or the same amount in another foreign currency. This covers all forms of currency, not only cash. This applies if you're travelling between Portugal and any non-European Union country. You don't need to declare currency if you're travelling to or from another European Union country. You'll be fined if you don't declare or give incorrect information. Foreign bank cards may not be accepted in smaller shops, restaurants, towns or rural areas. You can use Australian credit cards at larger hotels and shopping centres.

visa-preparation.fastest_entry: Visa-free Schengen short stay, normally up to 90 days in any 180-day period
visa-preparation.before_departure: Check the Portuguese mission/AIMA, Schengen day count and whether the trip is visitor, remote-worker or local work.
visa-preparation.useful_stay: Use the visitor route for short scouting; D8/D2 and other residence routes take a prepared dossier.
